A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPReD research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison; v2 adds an acknowledgments page.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotics and locomotion experiments, computational measurements, robustness tests and ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons and the supplementary experiments in Appendices C, F and G.

M1.justification: The SPReD-P and SPReD-E weighting mechanisms, ensemble architecture, objectives and training procedure remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight Fetch/Shadow Hand tasks and five locomotion tasks, including the same demonstration-quality and noisy-reward scenarios.

E2.justification: TD3, EnsTD3, Q-filter, EnsQ-filter, RLPD, AWAC, AWAC-p and AWAC-r remain in the corresponding benchmark comparisons. Comparator membership in the appendix analyses is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Interaction budgets, demonstration quantities, evaluation metrics, model configurations and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same training settings and evaluation over 25 test episodes.

E4.justification: The same analyses examine demonstration quality and quantity, noisy rewards, uncertainty estimators, Gaussian assumptions, gradient variance, adaptive weights, ensemble size, component contributions and normalization sensitivity. None is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed means and standard deviations in Tables 1 and 4 and the same uncertainty presentation in the figures. No run-count, seed or statistical-procedure changes are reported.

E6.justification: The tables and figures retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports FetchStack2 success rates of 0.920 ± 0.057 for SPReD-E and 0.064 ± 0.048 for RLPD in both versions. Figure 1 changes labeling and spacing, not the plotted findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemma 5.1, Properties 5.1–5.3 and the proofs and further derivations in Appendices B and C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about uncertainty-aware continuous regularization, reduced gradient variance, robustness and success-rate improvements of up to 14 times.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the discussion of later-stage learning slowdown, hyperparameter sensitivity, convergence analysis and the simulation-to-real gap.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, computational costs, demonstration-generation instructions and the code-availability statement are retained without revision.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and all 62 references retain the same cited works and research positioning. The added acknowledgments do not revise relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 8, Acknowledgments, identifying funding support, and corrects 'dash' to 'dashed' in several figure captions. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds numeric y-axis tick labels to the FetchPickAndPlace, FetchStack2 and ManipulateBlockRotate panels and adjusts panel spacing. Caption wording receives small corrections, and the acknowledgments page shifts subsequent pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited presentation and disclosure improvement: Figure 1's added y-axis labels make three panels easier to read, caption wording is corrected, and funding support is explicitly acknowledged. The methods, scientific evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged.
